solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son holding wicket planted in the earth

indicators.note: the son is said to hold the wicket, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written, the whole word
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A boy has a cricket stump in his hand while something is put into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed that has been scattered or set into soil to grow is said to have been sown.

clue.text: Imitation diamond that's sported by an Irishman?

parts.note: a sham is a fake or imitation
rock is slang for a diamond, as in an engagement ring

explanation.surface: A fake gem worn by an Irish man as jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: the three-leaved plant is Ireland's emblem, worn especially on St Patrick's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The clover-like national emblem of Ireland is traditionally pinned to the lapel by Irish people on St Patrick's Day.

clue.text: Blew his turn somewhat in card game

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A card player squandered a go during the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic trick-taking game for four players in two partnerships, forerunner of bridge.

clue.text: Nation left by reformation of Gaul

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

indicators.note: the word Gaul is formed again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A country abandoned after Gaul was reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as 'abandoned' but is the sailor's word for the left side; 'reformation of' hints at Europe's religious history but only shuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian republic beside Spain is a sovereign country.

clue.text: What traveller needs detective work finished by the next morning?

definitions.meaning: a small bag holding enough for one night away

definitions.text: detective work finished by the next morning?
definitions.meaning: an investigation solved in the space of one night, read literally

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a detective to wrap up the inquiry by dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A small suitcase packed for a one-night stay; read as two words, a case cracked in one night.

clue.text: Flower heads in the undergrowth, lying in pieces

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their opening letters, picked from the last five words

explanation.surface: Blooms that have been beheaded lie scattered in pieces among the undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes the first letter of each of the five words after 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-blooming bulb plant with cup-shaped blooms, famous in Holland.

clue.text: Little new in over-showy decoration for food

indicators.note: the small letter is placed in the word for over-showy

parts.note: garish means gaudy, too bright and showy
N is the short form, a little version, of new

explanation.surface: Not much fresh in a flashy dish topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside GARISH, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig of parsley or similar trimming added to a dish to make it look attractive.

clue.text: Common fund raised for diversionary rail link

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: a pool is money put together by several people

explanation.surface: Shared money collected to pay for a railway bypass.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop line is a stretch of track leaving the main line and rejoining it, letting trains pass.

clue.text: Arouse class with article in French

parts.note: a kind is a class or sort
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Stirring up a class by using a French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To set burning, and figuratively to stir up or awaken a feeling such as interest.

clue.text: A serious error in English is foolish

parts.note: a sin is a grave wrong

explanation.surface: Making a grave mistake in one's own language is idiotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and stupid, literally like an ass or donkey.

clue.text: Mostly great opening for Olympic movement

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: large means great in size

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Mostly a fine start for an Olympic sports event or campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of LARGE; 'opening for' takes O from Olympic. 'movement' looks athletic but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, broad section of a symphony or sonata is often marked with this Italian tempo term.

clue.text: Assessed faulty tread

indicators.note: a faulty word is one whose letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An inspector has judged a tyre's tread defective.
explanation.definitionFit: To have valued or graded something is to have judged its worth.

clue.text: Never — not ever — put out a pink serviette

indicators.note: the word ever is not wanted, so it is removed from never
put out signals the words a pink being disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists a pink table cloth must never, ever be laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes EVER from NEVER, leaving N; 'put out' rearranges A PINK to APKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth or paper square for wiping the mouth at table, called a serviette in Britain.

clue.text: Decorate or give title to National Trust

parts.note: to name something is to give it a title
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A choice between adorning a property or giving it a name for the heritage charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to adorn or embellish something with trimmings.

clue.text: Creator of steps in routine task old mathematical plotter follows

indicators.note: the plotter comes after the earlier pieces in the answer

parts.note: a chore is a dull everyday job
a grapher draws graphs of functions

explanation.surface: A dance designer's routine comes after a dreary chore and some maths plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creator of steps' and 'routine' both suggest dance, but 'routine task' is CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who devises the sequence of moves in a dance or ballet.

clue.text: Keep down work on all the papers

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Holding back work printed across every newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjugate or hold people under harsh authority.

clue.text: Strike at fixing pin

parts.note: a tack is a short nail or pin used to fasten something

explanation.surface: Hitting at a drawing pin to fix it in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault or hit out at someone, as a verb or a noun.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink I needed during several journeys back

indicators.note: the letter comes during, so inside, the other piece
back says the word for journeys is read in reverse

parts.note: trips are journeys, several of them

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a stiff drink during a series of homeward trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TRIPS into SPIRT, and 'during' puts I inside it, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled liquor such as whisky or gin is called a spirit.

clue.text: Get angry about France's no.1 weapon

indicators.note: the word for angering goes round the other piece

parts.note: rile means to anger or make cross

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper over the leading French arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled firearm fired from the shoulder.

clue.text: Greek character the volunteers wanted here

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek man pinning a 'volunteers wanted' sign up here.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's part-time volunteer army.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, written as a circle with a bar.

clue.text: Best European roofing slab lifted up

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tile is a slab laid on a roof

explanation.surface: A top-quality European roof tile has been lifted off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted up' reverses TILE to ELIT, followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: A select group regarded as superior, the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Football official leaving refused to be exploited

indicators.note: the official is leaving, so departs from the word refused

parts.note: ref is short for referee

explanation.surface: A referee, departing, declined to be taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken advantage of unfairly, as a person can be.

clue.text: Quiet little creature is a supporter of books?

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
an elf is a small mythical being

explanation.surface: A silent little sprite in a library propping up the volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a playful definition: a ledge holds books up.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board fixed to a wall or in a bookcase bears the weight of the volumes on it.

clue.text: Structure I have to store away

parts.note: an arch is a curved structure
've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: I need a building to keep things stashed in.
explanation.definitionFit: To file records or documents in a repository for keeping.

clue.text: Get untidy she-devil upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, the letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A wicked woman gets mussed up after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To make hair or clothing messy and disordered.

clue.text: Irritable when not finishing exam

indicators.note: the word is not finished, so loses its final letter

parts.note: testy means irritable or short-tempered

explanation.surface: A student is crabby about an unfinished paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A school assessment of knowledge or skill.
